questions.q: What does Beecham mean by a mistaken identity?
a: Living below your potential without knowing your true self
Pretending to be someone else to impress others
Believing you are better than your teammates
Adopting a persona that helps you win competitions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says settling for less than your best self amounts to a mistaken identity.

questions.q: How many bad days a month do top athletes have?
a: Three to six
One or two
Ten to twelve
Nearly every day
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites studies showing elite athletes log three to six rough days monthly.

questions.q: What does Beecham advise about perfectionism?
a: Accept failure and hard days as part of the process
Train harder until bad days disappear entirely
Compare yourself only with the best performers
Avoid goals that carry any risk of failure
questions.why: Lesson 2 says rough days belong to the process and perfectionism only makes people miserable.

questions.q: What did Aristotle say courage leads to?
a: Eudaimonia, a state of fulfillment and happiness
Wealth and recognition from your community
Freedom from all fear and uncertainty
Wisdom that comes only with old age
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Aristotle treated courage as the key virtue and tied it to eudaimonia, a state of fulfillment.

questions.q: How does Beecham suggest you overcome fear?
a: Seek motivation, get excited and act despite the fear
Wait until the fear fades before taking action
Avoid situations where failure is possible
Reason your way through every worst-case scenario
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends finding extrinsic motivation, getting excited about the journey and going after what scares you anyway.
